title: Wave planner: items touching the same subsystem must share a lane or sequence across waves — a sibling ship mid-batch changed a contract under a running lane
summary: Cycle-1484 (batch-20260816a): the context-fill CAP lane assumed a default 200K window for agy while its SIBLING context-fill telemetry lane shipped mid-batch the contract 'unmeasured families stay unmeasured' (fillpct_driverwindow_test.go) — the fresh test deterministically red'd the running lane. Partition menus key on exact-file overlap only; semantic coupling (same subsystem, disjoint files) is invisible to them.
root_cause: Menu partitioning is file-overlap-scoped; two items in one subsystem with disjoint file sets dispatch concurrently and one lane's landing changes semantics under the other.
fix: Cheap heuristic at wave planning: items sharing a subsystem prefix (id prefix family like context-fill-*/tokenopt-*, or files under one internal/<pkg>) either co-lane (multi-slug — AFTER multi-slug-lane-scope-reconciliation 0.87 lands) or defer the later one a wave. Log the deferral (no silent caps).
acceptance: Fixture: two same-prefix items plan into one lane or consecutive waves, logged.
connects_to: batching_partition_menus (exact-file-overlap design — this extends, not replaces)
